title: Why Aren’t Stocks Plunging?
gist: Teaser by Didier Darcet (Gavekal-IS) noting that despite blocked/disrupted Hormuz and Bab al Mandab straits, WTI at $90, building inflation and rising rates, the MSCI World has risen 9% since Gulf hostilities began on Feb 28, 2026. It asks what positive the market is pricing; the answer is paywalled.

insights.claim: As of October 2026 both the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al Mandab are blocked or severely disrupted following hostilities in the Persian Gulf that erupted on February 28, 2026.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Dual chokepoint disruption is a sustained supply shock for energy and shipping, not a transient spike.
insights.quote: The Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al Mandab are blocked—or at least severely disrupted.
insights.locator: The start of autumn is often

insights.claim: WTI crude oil is trading around US$90/bbl amid the Gulf disruption.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Oil at $90 feeds directly into inflation and rate pressure, shaping the macro backdrop for equities.
insights.quote: Crude oil is at US$90/bbl for WTI.
insights.locator: The start of autumn is often

insights.claim: Inflationary pressures are building and both short-term and long-term interest rates are rising, with clouds gathering over the global economy.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A stagflation-flavoured mix of higher energy costs and rising yields would normally compress equity valuations.
insights.quote: Short-term and long-term interest rates are rising.
insights.locator: The start of autumn is often

insights.claim: Despite chokepoint blockages, $90 oil, building inflation and rising rates — described as the perfect cocktail for a crash — global equities have risen rather than fallen.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Markets are pricing something positive beyond the headline risks; investors positioned for a crash have been wrong-footed.
insights.quote: The perfect cocktail for a stock-market crash.Yet the market is doing the opposite.
insights.locator: The start of autumn is often

insights.claim: The MSCI World index has risen 9% since hostilities erupted in the Persian Gulf on February 28, 2026.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Equities have looked through the geopolitical shock, a key data point for positioning and risk appetite.
insights.quote: global equities—as measured by the MSCI World index—have risen 9%
insights.locator: Yet the market is doing the opposite

insights.claim: The piece frames the key question as what the market sees as positive in the current situation, implying an underlying bullish driver the author goes on to identify (explanation behind paywall).
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors should seek the offsetting positive the market is discounting rather than assume equities are mispriced.
insights.quote: So what does the market see as positive in the current situation?
insights.locator: Yet the market is doing the opposite
